description: Approved current-worktree refactor; preserve existing PR0 changes; no commit/push/PR. Strengthen existing People.merge_persons/2 for scalar or list losers, transactional relationship reconciliation, explicit release-time normalization through canonical merge, tests and E2E. Sequencing: graph LR; merge --> release --> validation. Pending semantic clarification: completed step results in resumable workflow runs are simultaneously historical execution records and live replay inputs.

comments.text: Stopped before code edits per user escalation instruction. Semantic decision needed: completed Step.Run results are replay inputs for resumable runs (lib/zaq/engine/workflows/step_runner.ex:102-109); run steps snapshots are explicitly immutable even for in-progress runs (docs/services/workflows.md:367-369). Does historical preservation exclude all execution records belonging to nonterminal runs, allowing narrow typed rewrites there, or must those remain immutable and merging instead reject affected resumable runs? The latter adds a merge policy requiring approval; an alias-resolution layer would expand scope. No source/test/docs files changed; existing PR0 staged/unstaged changes preserved. Planned dependency chain: zaq-dln.3 -> zaq-dln.1 -> zaq-dln.2. Tests and quality checks not run because implementation is blocked before edits.

User decision: workflow execution snapshots and cached results remain unchanged, including resumable runs. Never block merge for these records, remap them, retry them, or introduce failure machinery. Deleted references may fail through existing behavior; retry is a user decision. Preserve actual relational references and narrowly typed live definitions/scheduled jobs only. Continue canonical merge plus thin release normalization.

BUILD supersedes prior scope: merge_persons/3 with default opts retains inactive redirects; nullable self FK, timestamp and original name/email; canonical old-ID reads, flat chains, protected deletion, excluded normal discovery. Historical workflow snapshots/results and approvals immutable. Small redirect schema migration replaces duplicate normalization migration; thin release operation defaults redirects. Add approved BO survivor merged-entry history. No other editors, status confirmed PR0-only. Conservative deletion policy: reject deleting a canonical survivor while redirect rows reference it.

Schema + canonical merge + release + BO history implemented. Dependency diamond is intentional: independent release and BO consumers both depend on canonical merge and converge at validation. Identity audit fixed raw Ingestion Person lookup, resource-query discovery and authorization, Record authorization, document permission filters, conversation ownership/history and routing identity. Workflow/Oban JSON and approval audit left unchanged. Initial E2E blocked by missing schema in E2E DB; applied schema-only migration to isolated E2E database. People E2E now 57/57 passing across Firefox/WebKit/Chromium. Focused tests 2 properties + 125 tests passing; broader related regression run exposed resource-query private-descriptor filtering and Record filter N+1, both being corrected. Initial mix q had only alias Credo suggestions, addressed.
